pr.title: Subscribe sessions to their pull requests in place of the loop skills
pr.head: a7203b5d6a574a307ec3e4348f01e081e03f9881

summary: Projector drives a pull request to a clean review with two kinds of agent work: a fixer, which answers review findings and merge conflicts with fix-pr, and a reviewer, which reviews each pushed head with review-pr. Until this stack, two skills kept that work going. start-watch-loop ran a watcher script, watch-threads.sh, in the conversation that opened a pull request. start-review-loop ran watch-prs.sh to review every pull request of the operator's. The operator is the GitHub account gh is signed in as.

The layer below, #386, adds the watch daemon: one background process per machine, project watch serve, that polls every pull request an agent session subscribes to and appends events for it to the session. A subscription is one line in the session's folder that names a pull request, or a repository, and a role: fix or review. An event is one line such as FINDING, NEW HEAD, or MOVED that ends with what the session should do.

This layer moves the skills onto that daemon. The skills that open or push a pull request subscribe the session to fix it with project watch add. review-pr subscribes the session to review the pull request it reviews, and the new review-repo subscribes the session to review a whole repository. The rules for acting on each event move out of the two loop skills into fix-pr and review-pr, and both loop skills and their watcher scripts are deleted. The docs, the website, and the generated AGENTS.md section follow. The layer above, #388, moves Projector's panel and Claude Code mod onto the daemon.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Session: one agent conversation and its subagents. Claude Code names it in CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. On another host, the top-level conversation picks an id and passes it as --session or PROJECTOR_SESSION.
  • Owner: the one session the daemon gives a pull request's events for a role. A subscription to the pull request beats one to its repository, and the newer one wins between equals.
  • Delivery: how events reach the session. project watch add ends with an events: line: mod (Claude Code's mod, in #388), stream (a running project watch stream), or none, with the command to start.
  • Fence: project review publish, move, and settle refuse when the head's lock no longer names their --loop, because the daemon handed the review to another session.

cards.title: Review status
cards.html: Projector review 5718931462 of a7203b5 requested changes with two P2 findings, both in prose: docs/cli.md still describes the old loops, and three edited Markdown lines are far wider than the lines around them. The full gate passed, as did npm run typecheck, lint, and build in web/.

groups.title: The plan records what the skills settled
groups.kicker: Section 9.2 of the watch-daemon plan, a deferred question, and two more rows in the file table
intro: The plan, docs/projects/watch-daemon/readme.md, already describes the skills in § 2.10. This layer adds § 9.2, which records the choices that building the skills settled. Read it first, because the skill groups below carry those choices out.

A new open question in § 7 covers a stack whose layers end up with different fix owners. Ownership is per pull request, but one subagent fixes a whole stack, so fix-pr stops on such a MOVED and asks the user.

files.note: New § 9.2, a deferred question in § 7, and two rows in § 2.12's file table.

groups.title: Pushing a pull request subscribes the session to fix it
groups.kicker: fix-pr, implement, and spec subscribe with project watch add and act on fix events
intro: Each skill that opens or pushes a pull request now runs project watch add owner/repo#number after the push, for every layer of a stack. The fix role is the default. The skill skips the command when watch.auto_start is false, and reads the events: line to learn whether something delivers the session's events. Only the top-level conversation starts project watch stream, because a subagent's processes end when it returns.

fix-pr gains two sections. Subscribe the session to the pull request holds the subscription rules that implement and spec cite. Act on the session's events takes over the old watch loop's rules: what each fix event means, one subagent per pull request named fix-<number> or fix-stack-<number>, and the report of clean state and stack readiness.
Because a subagent's commands carry the session's id, implement drops its rule to hand a pull request up to the top-level conversation.

checks.text: Each command, flag, and quoted output line matches add_watch_parser and watch_delivery in src/projector/cli.py, and each event's action text matches route_fix and closing_actions in src/projector/watch.py, read at this head.

files.note: New sections for subscribing and for acting on events, plus wording that names a review or the watch daemon where it named a loop.
The hand-over subscribes the session and reports the events: line, in place of starting or joining a watch loop.
A plan's pull request subscribes the session to fix it, as fix-pr describes.

groups.title: Reviewing subscribes the session to review
groups.kicker: review-pr subscribes after setup and always passes --loop; review-repo replaces start-review-loop
intro: review-pr now subscribes the session to review the pull request after project review setup succeeds. Setup takes a lock on the head first, so the daemon sees a review in flight and announces nothing for the head under review. Every project review command passes the session's id as --loop, so each session keeps its own record of published reviews, and a review a person asks for can be incremental too.

The skill gains Act on the session's review events and Stop when the review moves to another session. They cover NEW PR, NEW HEAD, a stalled review, RESPONDED, MOVED, and closing. They also cover the fence, which tells a reviewer whose review was handed over to stop rather than run setup again.

review-repo is new. It subscribes the session to review every open pull request the operator wrote or that requests the operator's review, runs project review rules once to warn about missing permissions, and starts a review-<number> subagent for each event. A subagent it starts skips the per-pull-request subscription, so stopping the repository review leaves nothing subscribed.

checks.text: tests/test_review.py reads the list of commands that take --loop and --model from review-pr and checks that it names every project review command. The suite passed at this head.

files.note: Subscription, the --loop rule, event handling, and the hand-over fence.
New skill: subscribe to a repository's reviews, what that covers, and how to stop.

groups.title: The loop skills and their watchers are deleted
intro: With every rule now in fix-pr or review-pr, the two loop skills and their watcher scripts go. A loop that a session started before upgrading keeps running from the old plugin version's folder until the session ends. Those scripts call only gh, and project loop stays for one release.

checks.text: No user-facing document tells an upgrading user what happens to a loop that is already running. The plan's rollout step 3 covers it. The review body suggests a short note in docs/plugins.md.

groups.title: Tests follow the removed files
groups.kicker: Packaging guard, rewritten skill tests, and the watcher tests' removal
intro: tests/test_packaging.py publishes review-repo in place of both loop skills. Its new guard fails when any file under skills/ names a removed loop skill, a watcher script, project loop, or --tracked. The tests in tests/test_review.py that read the loop skill now read review-pr and review-repo. tests/test_watchers.py goes with the scripts, because #386 ported its cases to tests/test_watch.py. Two docstrings in src/projector/watch.py stop naming the scripts.
